questions.q: What hidden assumption does standard RLHF depend on?
options: That the reward model and the policy are always the same network
That the model being trained has no knowledge of being evaluated
That the human providing feedback can reliably tell which of two outputs is actually better
That human feedback is only ever needed once, at the very start of training
questions.explain: RLHF's entire pipeline rests on human preference judgments tracking real quality; once that stops holding, the learned reward model stops being a trustworthy target.

questions.q: Why does the oversight problem get worse as model capability increases, rather than being fixed by hiring better evaluators?
options: Better evaluators always cost significantly more money regardless of the task
As models approach and exceed the top of human expertise in a domain, the pool of humans who can out-evaluate the model shrinks toward zero no matter how carefully they're selected
Models become less willing to accept any human feedback at all
Evaluators become more capable at exactly the same rate models do
questions.explain: Expert evaluators help at a given capability level, but the trend is that model capability keeps climbing while the supply of humans who can verify work at that level does not scale with it.

questions.q: Which of these best defines scalable oversight as a research problem?
options: A technique for making training runs finish faster on less hardware
Making models evaluate themselves instead of using any human input
Developing methods to supervise AI systems effectively on tasks where unaided human judgment doesn't reliably scale to the task's difficulty
Reducing the number of human reviewers needed for any task
questions.explain: Scalable oversight specifically targets getting trustworthy supervisory signal on the hardest tasks, not simply cutting humans out of the loop.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the 'sandwiching' experimental design used in Anthropic's scalable oversight research?
options: To deliberately choose tasks where specialists succeed but unaided humans and current models both fail, so researchers can measure whether a proposed oversight method actually closes that gap
To prevent models from ever seeing the same prompt twice
To make evaluation faster by skipping human review entirely
To combine two separate reward models into a single larger one
questions.explain: Sandwiching creates a controlled gap between unaided human/model performance and specialist performance, giving researchers a measurable target for whether an oversight method helps.

questions.q: How does scalable oversight differ from the capability/safety evaluations covered in Chapter 3?
options: Scalable oversight only applies to image-generation models
Evaluations require more compute than any scalable oversight method
They are the same thing described with different names
Evaluations ask what a model can do and whether that's dangerous; scalable oversight asks whether we can even tell if the model did a specific task well when we can't do that task well ourselves
questions.explain: Evaluation and scalable oversight address different layers of the problem: evaluation measures capability, while scalable oversight addresses whether supervisory judgment itself can be trusted.
